Subject: Finly — onboarding for app integration (SDK + migration)

Hi Vanessa,

We're moving forward with Redwood for our in-app assistant and want to land the integration this quarter. Can you send a plain checklist for: SDK setup, sample code, recommended per-request timeouts & retries, and an endpoint migration window (we have a short maintenance window on weekends)? Also flag anything procurement needs from our side — I'll loop them in.

High-level constraints:
- Average request size: ~600 tokens, spikes to 2k tokens on longer flows
- Hard P95 latency target: 300ms for search and short completions; ok for longer async jobs
- We'll start in us-west and later expand to eu-central

Attaching a short architecture sketch in a follow-up. Thanks — want to kick off next week if possible.

Alex Gomez
Head of Engineering, Finly

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Alex — quick technical starter below plus attached SDK samples (sdk-samples-v1.zip). Please use the sandbox keys in the README and don't reuse them in prod.

Quick SDK setup (Node example):
- npm i @redwood/inference-sdk
- export REDWOOD_API_KEY="sandbox-xxx"
- minimal sample:

  const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference-sdk');
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, region: 'us-west' });

  async function simplePrompt() {
    const res = await client.generate({
      model: 'redwood-mini-1',
      prompt: 'Summarize the user message',
      max_tokens: 300,
      temperature: 0.2
    });
    console.log(res.text);
  }

Endpoint migration notes (runbook highlights):
- Cutover window: perform staged traffic shift (5/25/70%) across two hours during low traffic weekend slot
- Canary validation: 100 requests/s smoke tests for each shard; verify KV cache warmup for long sessions
- Fallback: immediate rollback to former endpoint + circuit-breaker if error rate > 5% or 429s sustained > 10s

Retries & timeouts (recommended starter):
- Connection timeout: 2000ms
- Header handshake/read timeout: 35000ms (for long responses)
- Client retries: 3 attempts, exponential backoff (base=300ms) with full jitter, max backoff 8s
- Idempotency: attach request_id for generate calls that may be retried to avoid duplicate billing for side-effectful ops

Attachments: sdk-samples-v1.zip (contains README, Node + Python snippets, smoke-test harness)

Happy to walk through the sample bundle in kickoff.

—Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Adding a few low-level resiliency & rate-control items we recommend for your engineers to implement client-side before cutover:

Retries + backoff:
- Use retryable status list: [429, 502, 503, 504]
- Backoff algorithm: exponential with full jitter; e.g., attemptDelay = random(0, base * 2^attempt)
- Cap attempts to 3 for interactive flows; longer async jobs can be retried up to 5 with idempotency keys

Timeouts:
- TCP connect: 1500–2000ms
- First byte/read: 10s for chat/small completions, 30–45s for long generation flows

Streaming behaviors:
- For streaming endpoints, use a 65s idle heartbeat to close stalled streams and attempt reconnect with resume token when possible

Rate limiting & tokens:
- Implement a local token-bucket rate limiter set to your expected steady-state RPS (burst buffer = 2x)
- On 429: read Retry-After header. If absent, apply incremental backoff with full jitter and decrement local burst allowance
- When moving to production, request quota bump for sustained >10k tokens/s to avoid throttling during peak jobs

Observability:
- Emit metrics: request_latency_ms, request_retries, 429_count, tokens_consumed per route; capture request_id header for trace back

If you want, I'll share a tiny middleware snippet you can drop into your HTTP client (Node/Go).

—Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
